title: Explore local Codex conversation history
summary: List, show, search, export, resolve exact persisted task metadata, or inspect content-free completed-turn activity for local Codex tasks through the documented App Server interface.
use_when: The user wants to inspect, query, search, or export Codex tasks stored on this machine.
Another local product needs typed user/assistant conversation history with stable source references.
Another local product needs exact persisted task metadata, including the recorded working directory, for one canonical machine-local thread reference.
A local product needs exact completed-turn message scope and content-free evidence of completed Codex file changes, including recovery from a missed hook event.
do_not_use_when: The request is to continue, mutate, archive, delete, or send a message to a live Codex task.
The request requires reasoning traces, tool payloads, approvals, or raw Codex storage.
The user wants a model to interpret the conversations rather than retrieve them.
outcome: A complete requested App Server view normalized to user and assistant text, an exact persisted task summary for a canonical machine-local thread reference, or an explicit completed-turn activity view containing message counts and stable completed-file-change references without paths or diffs.
effects: List, show, search, export, activity, and doctor launch a short-lived local Codex App Server in a private process group, read its state-database view, and terminate that launch's inherited descendants on exit.
An exact-summary library call returns persisted task metadata, including the recorded working directory, only to its local caller and does not change CLI or activity output.
Show, search, and export can write sensitive user and assistant transcript text to the caller's terminal or redirected output; activity writes only counts, timing/status, and stable references.
The explicit refresh command allows App Server to scan its own logs and repair its own metadata; no other command enables that behavior.
authority: Codex App Server owns task discovery, persisted-storage compatibility, pagination, metadata, and full-history availability.
Conversations owns filters, normalized user/assistant output, stable references, copied-item deduplication, and failure-on-incomplete behavior.
Observed runtime status belongs to the newly launched App Server process and is not machine-wide liveness authority.
success: Every requested active and archived page completes through App Server.
Full-history operations complete through turn pagination or the explicit legacy fallback without raw-storage access.

An exact summary lookup requires a matching stable host identity, finds the thread exactly once across active and archived state-database metadata, and returns its recorded working directory without loading turns.
JSON output excludes reasoning, tool, approval, command, file-path, diff, and internal item payloads.
Activity accepts only a completed turn with a completion timestamp, validates every counted file-change entry, and fails when a session hint resolves the turn in multiple lineage members.
The short-lived launch and its inherited descendants do not remain running after the operation.
failure_and_recovery: A protocol error, timeout, unreadable page, or unsupported full-history record fails the operation instead of returning an incomplete normal result.
Use `conversations doctor` to inspect the selected CLI and recorded-version mismatch before changing installations.
Run `conversations refresh` only when App Server metadata repair is intended.
privacy: Task titles, working directories, normalized transcript text, stable activity references, and activity counts can be private.
The default macOS host reference is a one-way platform-identity hash; the raw hardware UUID is never exposed or retained, and an identity read failure stops the operation.
Conversations sends no transcript to a model or network service of its own, but redirected stdout becomes caller-owned retained data.
Interactive CLI calls inherit App Server stderr by default; privacy-sensitive embedded or scheduled callers must select the suppression policy when their logs cannot retain Codex diagnostics.

interfaces.label: Resolve exact task metadata from Rust

does_not_authorize: Reading Codex JSONL or SQLite storage directly.
Continuing, mutating, archiving, deleting, or messaging any Codex task.
Sending or publishing exported transcript text, or interpreting it with a model.
